jobs.description_text: We’re looking for a Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer to lead Reddit’s next-generation user understanding initiative: building a unified, high-fidelity representation of each user that powers personalization across the platform. jobs.title: Senior Staff Engineer - AI Workloads & Storage

We are building the next generation of NAND/SSD storage systems designed for the demands of large-scale AI. As the compute cost of transformer inference falls, the bottleneck is shifting to how quickly and efficiently we can move model weights, KV cache, and activations through the storage hierarchy - and NAND flash and SSDs are increasingly the tier where that data lives. Our focus is on making SSDs first-class citizens in the AI data path, from the NAND media and flash-translation layer up through NVMe and networked storage. We are looking for a Sr Staff Engineer who lives at the intersection of AI inference systems and storage/systems software . This is a hands-on technical leadership role: you will characterize real AI workloads, translate what you learn into architecture, and drive that direction across inference, platform, and hardware teams. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM Anduril’s Additive Manufacturing team is a high-speed development lab supporting some of our highest-priority programs. We turn evolving designs into physical hardware that engineers can test, learn from, and iterate on immediately. This is not a production print farm. We operate in a high-mix, low-volume prototype environment where quality, technical judgment, and speed matter more than pushing identical parts through a machine. Our technicians work directly with design engineers across Anduril, helping determine how a part should be built—not simply printing whatever lands in the queue. We’re looking for an experienced FDM specialist to become the team’s go-to technical owner for our FDM capability. ABOUT THE JOB You’ll own FDM prototype builds from initial request through finished hardware. That means much more than starting a printer… You’ll review incoming CAD, understand what the engineer is trying to accomplish, identify printability issues, select materials and build strategies, prepare custom toolpaths, operate and calibrate equipment, troubleshoot failures, post-process parts, and verify that the finished hardware meets the original need. You’ll own a fleet of eight FDM systems, including four industrial machines, while managing a dynamic queue of roughly 10–20 active jobs. jobs.description_text: About the team Air Dominance & Strike designs, builds, and flies autonomous air vehicles — from collaborative combat aircraft to expendable cruise missiles to counter-UAS interceptors. Our vehicles move from whiteboard to first flight on timelines that traditional primes consider impossible, which means our design cycles live or die on how fast we can close the iteration loop and begin testing. The Anduril AI-Engineering team exists to collapse that loop. We are engineers first. We work from engineering first principles and unlock capability through machine learning. We are building to scale across design, analysis, test, and program execution, with agent pipelines and tooling that carry across programs. About the job We are looking for an Agentic AI Engineer to automate engineering workflows, build new capability through agents, and improve how engineers access and act on their data. Our R&D work runs through tools of varying fidelity, from empirical methods and low-order models to high-fidelity solvers. You will chain those tools into automated flows that carry a design through analysis to build and then back into the next iteration. You will own agent pipelines end to end: orchestration logic, tool and data integrations, evaluation harnesses, and guardrails. Much of the work is getting agents to drive legacy engineering software which were built for human operators rather than programmatic control. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM Discovery is Anduril's team for the hard concepts: the ones that are not yet proven or built. We work with hardware and software engineering teams across the company, driving cross-functional collaboration across different business lines. ABOUT THE JOB We are building an expeditionary force: a small group of engineers who want to do big, new, hard things and who move into unfamiliar territory as a matter of course. As a Discovery Engineer you pick up a concept nobody has proven, learn whatever domain it lives in, build the analysis or prototype that tests it, and get to an answer. The problems change; the approach does not: reason from first principles, do the work, check it, and reach a solution. You are not hired for a particular skill set. You are hired for a record of getting engaged in problems across different areas, being analytic, testing new concepts, and getting to solutions. You are also the adversary to our own ideas. The rigor that validates a good concept is the same rigor that kills a bad one early, while it is still cheap, and you apply it to your own work first.
